findings.issue_text: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291, the expanded-reply username link has its light and dark values swapped/wrong: the light-theme value was changed from 30% to 70% lightness and the dark value is 30% instead of 70%, causing the bold username to render near-invisible (~2:1 contrast on white) in the default light theme and near-invisible (~1.9:1 against the dark background) in dark themes, while also breaking consistency with the 30/70 pattern used for the identical username elsewhere in the PR (e.g., aside.quote .title and common/base/topic-post.scss:15)

In app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss:239, the badge background was converted/adapted for dark theme but the paired text color (`&[href] { color: $secondary; }` at ~241) was left unchanged, so the text color was not adapted along with the background

In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 (the bolded `a` link in the replies block), the light/dark pair is inverted: 30% primary became `dark-light-choose(70% primary, 30% secondary)` when it should be `(30% primary, 70% secondary)`, causing sub-AA contrast in both themes (~1.9:1 on white in light themes, ~2.7:1 on dark background) for a clickable element.

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 (`.custom-message-length`), both arguments are flipped: the light value went 70% → 30% and the dark value is 70% instead of 30%, deviating from the correctly converted identical desktop rule (desktop/modal.scss:94); hint text renders much darker than before in light themes and much brighter than intended in dark themes.

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 (`h3` topic title in the suggested-topics block), the light value changed 20% → 50% while the desktop counterpart (desktop/topic-post.scss:321) correctly keeps 20/80, making mobile light-theme topic titles noticeably lighter than before and inconsistent with desktop.

In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 and app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497 (user card `.name`), the light value changed 30% → 50% in both files, lightening the displayed name in light themes, which is out of scope for a dark-theme PR; may be a deliberate unification with `.title` (50%) and needs author confirmation of intent.

In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291, the bold `a` in the topic-map block has swapped arguments in dark-light-choose: the light value uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) instead of 30%, changing the light-theme bold link from near-black to a very light gray with significant contrast loss (likely a WCAG failure)

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102, .custom-message-length has swapped arguments in dark-light-choose (30%/70% instead of the correct 70%/30% used in desktop/modal.scss:94), making mobile light-theme hint text render much darker than before and inconsistently with desktop

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182, the topic-map h3 light value changed from 20% to 50% (50%/50%), while the same heading at desktop/topic-post.scss:320 correctly keeps 20%/80%, causing the mobile light-theme heading to lose contrast relative to both its prior value and the desktop rendering

In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 and app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497, the profile .name light value changed from 30% to 50% (50%/50%), while .name in common/base/user.scss:123 keeps 30%/70%, making light-theme profile names render lighter than before

In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291, the light/dark pair was swapped: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` instead of `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, washing out the bold link in light themes (~#636363 to ~#bdbdbd) and dropping dark-theme contrast to ~2.8:1

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182, the mobile topic-map h3 light value was changed from 20% to 50% (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of 20%/80%), washing out the heading in light themes, dimming it in dark themes, and silently diverging from the desktop counterpart at desktop/topic-post.scss:320

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102, the `.custom-message-length` pair is inverted vs. desktop: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` instead of `dark-light-choose(70%, 30%)` as correctly kept in desktop/modal.scss:94, making the modal hint text darker than designed in light themes and brighter than designed in dark themes

In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 and app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497, the profile header `.name` light value changed from 30% to 50% (`dark-light-choose(50%, 50%)` instead of 30%/70% as kept in common/base/user.scss), washing out the light-theme display name (~#636363 to ~#919191), dimming the dark theme, and disagreeing with the user-card name

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss:175, the adjacent pre-existing rule `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` is left untouched by the sweep; `darken($primary, ...)` produces dark composer text on a dark background in dark color schemes and should be converted to the `dark-light-choose` style as a follow-up

In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291, both branches of the dark-light-choose conversion are wrong: the light value was rewritten from 30% to 70% (degrading the bold link to near-white-on-white contrast in light themes) and the dark branch uses 30% lightness of $secondary instead of 70%, so the link is low-contrast in both light and dark themes; it should be (30%, 70%)

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102, the .custom-message-length branches are inverted compared to its desktop twin: the old value 70% was converted to (30%, 70%) while the identical rule in desktop/modal.scss:94 was correctly converted to (70%, 30%), making hint text go from light gray to near-black in light themes and getting 70% instead of 30% in dark themes

In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522, the .name light value was changed from 30% to 50%, making the new declaration byte-identical to the adjacent .title's (apparently pasted from the neighboring line), so the profile name loses its emphasis in light themes; the dark branch should be 70% as in the correct conversion at common/base/user.scss:~124
In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497, the same .name slip occurs in the mobile twin: 30% was converted to (50%, 50%), duplicating .title

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182, the h3 light value was changed from 20% to 50%, becoming (50%, 50%) identical to the h4 directly below it, while the desktop twin at desktop/topic-post.scss:321 correctly keeps (20%, 80%); title text renders lighter than designed in light themes and dimmer in dark themes

No shared helper exists for the converted dark-light-choose idiom, leaving 100+ hand-maintained copies where the 100−X complement is transcribed by hand at each call site (the exact failure mode behind the five transcription errors); a single function like primary-scale($l) returning dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $l), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $l)) would make the complement structural and provide one adjustment point

Desktop/mobile twin rules were edited independently, and 3 pairs diverged (.custom-message-length in modal, .name/.title in user, h3/h4 in topic-post); rules that don't differ across breakpoints should live in common/ so a color fix only needs to exist once

In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss:175, the fix is incomplete within the same rule block: the PR converts the .wmd-input:disabled backgrounds (lines 168, 172) but leaves the enabled input's color: darken($primary, 40%) untouched, which darkens composer input text into a dim gray on dark backgrounds — the same class of dark-theme contrast bug in the adjacent rule

In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-list.scss:39-40, .fa-thumb-tack.unpinned is a no-op duplicate carrying a color declaration byte-identical to the .fa-thumb-tack base rule (before and after the PR), so it can never have an effect; the PR duplicated the new ~100-char expression into both and the dead declaration should be dropped

In app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss:89, dark-light-choose may not resolve in the embed entry point: embed.css.scss compiles through a separate entry point from the main bundle and the visible context shows no prior dark-light-* usage, so if the import chain doesn't include the function definition, embed stylesheet compilation fails and all embeds are unstyled; worth a compile check

app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:~291 — light/dark values are slot-swapped: the original `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was rewritten as `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, silently changing the light-theme value from 30% to 70% and giving the dark value 30% instead of the required 70% (the transformation was applied backwards for this line), making the bold replies/quote-expansion link near-illegible in both themes (~2:1 contrast in light themes and ~2.7:1 in dark themes, failing WCAG AA) in the most-trafficked element of normal topic browsing
One place in the PR pairs a changed background with an unchanged foreground, breaking the light/dark complement invariant

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102, the .custom-message-length branches are inverted compared to its desktop twin: the old value 70% was converted to (30%, 70%) while the identical rule in desktop/modal.scss:94 was correctly converted to (70%, 30%), making hint text go from light gray to near-black in light themes and getting 70% instead of 30% in dark themes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows desktop/modal.scss changes `.custom-message-length` from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, while mobile/modal.scss changes the same selector from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This is an inverted light/dark choice compared to desktop and compared to the original intent (70% lightness), so the mobile hint text will render much darker in the light theme and much lighter in the dark theme than intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522, the .name light value was changed from 30% to 50%, making the new declaration byte-identical to the adjacent .title's (apparently pasted from the neighboring line), so the profile name loses its emphasis in light themes; the dark branch should be 70% as in the correct conversion at common/base/user.scss:~124

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss the `.name` color changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which makes it byte-identical to the adjacent `.title` rule (also `...50%/50%`). This is inconsistent with the corresponding conversion in common/base/user.scss where `.name` uses `dark-light-choose(...30%, ...70%)`, suggesting an accidental paste and a likely visual regression (loss of emphasis).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497, the same .name slip occurs in the mobile twin: 30% was converted to (50%, 50%), duplicating .title

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss that `.name` was changed from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, while `.title` is also set to the same `50%/50%` value. This duplicates `.title` styling and is inconsistent with the analogous change in common/base/user.scss where `.name` maps `30%` to `dark-light-choose(...30%, ...70%)`, indicating a likely erroneous conversion that would cause a UI color regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182, the h3 light value was changed from 20% to 50%, becoming (50%, 50%) identical to the h4 directly below it, while the desktop twin at desktop/topic-post.scss:321 correctly keeps (20%, 80%); title text renders lighter than designed in light themes and dimmer in dark themes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss within `a.star h3` the color changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, while the immediately following `h4` also uses `...50%/50%`. This makes `h3` and `h4` identical in color on mobile and is inconsistent with the desktop counterpart (`desktop/topic-post.scss` `a.star h3` uses `dark-light-choose(...20%, ...80%)`). This is a concrete, diff-introduced visual regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No shared helper exists for the converted dark-light-choose idiom, leaving 100+ hand-maintained copies where the 100−X complement is transcribed by hand at each call site (the exact failure mode behind the five transcription errors); a single function like primary-scale($l) returning dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $l), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $l)) would make the complement structural and provide one adjustment point

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows many repeated, hand-written conversions from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: L)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: L), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: ...))` across numerous files, with the secondary lightness manually specified at each call site (e.g., 40/60, 30/70, 75/25, etc.). The diff does not introduce any shared SCSS helper/mixin/function to encode the complement structurally, so the finding about maintainability and a single adjustment point is diff-grounded. The claim that manual transcription can lead to mistakes is also supported by apparent inconsistencies in the diff (e.g., `desktop/topic-post.scss` changes an `a` color from primary lightness 30% to a `dark-light-choose` using primary 70%/secondary 30%, and `mobile/modal.scss` uses primary 30%/secondary 70% where most analogous cases use primary 70%/secondary 30%), suggesting the risk is real even if not strictly a functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Desktop/mobile twin rules were edited independently, and 3 pairs diverged (.custom-message-length in modal, .name/.title in user, h3/h4 in topic-post); rules that don't differ across breakpoints should live in common/ so a color fix only needs to exist once

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated desktop vs mobile styling being updated separately and at least two selector pairs now diverge: `.custom-message-length` differs between `desktop/modal.scss` (uses `dark-light-choose(...70%..., ...30%...)`) and `mobile/modal.scss` (uses `dark-light-choose(...30%..., ...70%...)`), and `a.star h3` differs between `desktop/topic-post.scss` (20%/80%) and `mobile/topic-post.scss` (50%/50%). The finding’s broader point about consolidating non-breakpoint-specific rules to avoid duplicate fixes is a valid maintainability concern grounded in these differences, though the specific claim about `.name/.title in user` diverging between desktop and mobile is not clearly supported (they appear the same in both files after the change).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss:175, the fix is incomplete within the same rule block: the PR converts the .wmd-input:disabled backgrounds (lines 168, 172) but leaves the enabled input's color: darken($primary, 40%) untouched, which darkens composer input text into a dim gray on dark backgrounds — the same class of dark-theme contrast bug in the adjacent rule

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss` updates the disabled backgrounds to `dark-light-choose(...)` (for `#reply-title:disabled` and `.wmd-input:disabled`) but leaves the enabled `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` unchanged within the same block. That is a concrete, diff-adjacent inconsistency with the PR’s broader pattern of replacing theme-sensitive color transforms with `dark-light-choose(...)`. However, the claim that this *definitely* causes poor contrast on dark themes cannot be verified from the diff alone (it depends on how `$primary` is defined in dark themes), so it’s better treated as an incomplete theming adjustment rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-list.scss:39-40, .fa-thumb-tack.unpinned is a no-op duplicate carrying a color declaration byte-identical to the .fa-thumb-tack base rule (before and after the PR), so it can never have an effect; the PR duplicated the new ~100-char expression into both and the dead declaration should be dropped

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-list.scss, the diff shows both `.fa-thumb-tack` and `.fa-thumb-tack.unpinned` set the exact same `color` value (after the PR, both use the same `dark-light-choose(scale-color(...), scale-color(...))` expression). Since `.fa-thumb-tack.unpinned` only matches a subset of `.fa-thumb-tack` and assigns an identical value, it does not change the computed style and is redundant duplication introduced/continued by this change (a maintainability issue rather than a functional bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss:89, dark-light-choose may not resolve in the embed entry point: embed.css.scss compiles through a separate entry point from the main bundle and the visible context shows no prior dark-light-* usage, so if the import chain doesn't include the function definition, embed stylesheet compilation fails and all embeds are unstyled; worth a compile check

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows replacing `scale-color(...)` with `dark-light-choose(...)` in `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` (e.g., the `a.new-user` rule). It does not show the embed entry point’s import chain or whether `dark-light-choose` is defined/available there, so the claim that embed compilation will fail cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:~291 — light/dark values are slot-swapped: the original `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was rewritten as `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, silently changing the light-theme value from 30% to 70% and giving the dark value 30% instead of the required 70% (the transformation was applied backwards for this line), making the bold replies/quote-expansion link near-illegible in both themes (~2:1 contrast in light themes and ~2.7:1 in dark themes, failing WCAG AA) in the most-trafficked element of normal topic browsing
matched_golden_ids: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the exact same change in `.topic-meta-data h5 a`: replacing `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, explicitly noting the light-theme lightness shift from 30% to 70% (an inversion) and that the values are effectively swapped/misapplied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: One place in the PR pairs a changed background with an unchanged foreground, breaking the light/dark complement invariant

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain at least one instance where a background is changed to use `dark-light-choose(...)` but the foreground is left unchanged: in `app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/badges.css.scss`, `background-color` is changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, while the nested `&[href] { color: $secondary; }` remains unchanged. This is a concrete mismatch that could undermine the intended light/dark pairing/contrast strategy, though whether it actually "breaks" contrast cannot be proven from the diff alone without knowing the theme variable values.
